headline: Conservation Pass Required for Valley Entry
reservation: A Kananaskis Conservation Pass is required for all vehicles stopping within the region, purchasable online or at visitor centers. This is a vehicle-based fee separate from any camping reservations or Alberta provincial park fees found elsewhere.

days.title: Peter Lougheed Lakes

stops.name: Upper Kananaskis Lake
stops.detail: Walk the shoreline trail for views of Mount Lyautey and access to several hidden waterfall feeders.

stops.name: Lower Kananaskis Lake
stops.detail: A prime location for viewing the Highwood Pass peaks reflected in the calmer morning waters.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours from Canmore via Smith Dorrien or Highway 40; conditions vary.
days.note: Highwood Pass is subject to a seasonal wildlife closure from December to mid-June.

days.title: Spray Valley Vistas

stops.name: Spray Lakes Reservoir
stops.detail: Follow the gravel Smith-Dorrien Trail for expansive views of the jagged peaks flanking this massive waterway.

stops.name: Mount Engadine Meadow
stops.detail: Watch for resident moose in the valley bottom marshes from the designated pull-offs near the lodge.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours if navigating the unpaved sections of the Smith-Dorrien Trail.
days.note: Dust and washboard conditions are common on secondary gravel roads; reduce speed.

days.title: Sibbald and Elbow Gateway

stops.name: Forget-Me-Not Pond
stops.detail: Visit this emerald pond at the end of Highway 66 for a gentle walk beneath the Nihahi Ridge.

stops.name: Elbow Falls
stops.detail: Witness the power of the Elbow River as it drops into a rocky gorge near the Bragg Creek entry point.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from Calgary; Highway 66 is paved but narrow.
days.note: The Elbow Falls area can be exceptionally busy on summer weekends; visit early.

intel.title: Limited Valley Services
intel.text: The Fortress Junction Service Centre is the only fuel point within the heart of Kananaskis on Highway 40. Always enter the region from Calgary or Canmore with a full tank.

intel.title: Fragmented Reception
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent in the Spray Valley and highly unreliable in the Peter Lougheed back-country. Emergency phones are located at select day-use areas and visitor centers.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The northern section of Highway 40 (Highwood Pass) and Highway 66 have winter closures for wildlife corridors. Check the Alberta 511 system for gate status before planning a through-drive.

intel.title: Wildlife Movement
intel.text: Dawn and dusk are peak times for bear and moose activity along the roadsides. Expect slower travel speeds if wildlife is present and maintain a respectful distance.

intel.title: Day-Use Congestion
intel.text: Popular spots like Barrier Lake and Elbow Falls often reach vehicle capacity by mid-morning. Have a secondary trail in mind to avoid circling lots.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at YYC, stock up on bear-safe storage in Calgary, and proceed to Bragg Creek or Canmore basecamp.
plan.vehicle: SUVs are recommended for the gravel Smith-Dorrien Trail; check rental insurance for unpaved road coverage.
plan.goldenHour: Barrier Lake Lookout for sunset views over the front ranges; check local tables for autumn shifts.
